sentences.text: The species Palintropus retusus is known from a single proximal coracoid bone discovered in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.

A 2009 cladistic analysis by Longrich and colleagues suggested Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis and belongs in the family Palintropiformes, whereas the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group and family as Quercymegapodiidae and classifies it under the class Reptilia.
In contrast, the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group and family assigned to Palintropus as Quercymegapodiidae and classifies it under the class Reptilia.
Some researchers believe Palintropus is an early member of the Charadriiformes, similar to birds of the Western Interior Seaway, while others note its potential link to subtropical coastlands.
An alternate theory suggests Palintropus is a galliform, possibly a quercymegapodiid, an alternative view that aligns with other classification suggestions.
